header.name: Networks and Systems Security
header.description: This course derives the best elements from two existing courses Network Security (CSE 550) and Security Engineering (CSE 352/552). The courses would largely cover topics like access controls (DAC/MAC), software vulnerabilities -- buffer overflow exploits, string vulnerabilities, heap vulnerabilities, ROP/ret2libc, crytographic system libraries and frameworks, network security primitives at various layers -- wifi exploits and security, L3 security framework, centralized and distributed authentication systems, DoS/DDoS attacks, firewalls, VPNs

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Abilitiy to identify of basic system level vulnerabilities, and writing applications to make sure to avoid them.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to design and implement various system and network access control and security postures.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to design and implement various security postures using system and network based cryptographic frameworks like OpenSSL.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to describe in depth various infrastructure vulnerabilities and security postures to circumvent those.

lecture_topics: Basics of systems and network security

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment:
Assignment – basic access controls, designing your own small kernel firewall, setting up access controls
Lab – Linux IPTables/FreeBSD PF

lecture_topics: Basic buffer overflow vulnerabilities - stack smashing
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment -- basic stack overflow vulnerability/bypassing stack smashing protection advanced vulnerability ROP
Lab – Using tools to craft your own payloads, testing various kernel level frameworks for preventing against such attacks.

lecture_topics: Basics of crypto primitives to ensure, confidentiality, integrity and authentication - shared and public key ciphers
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Lab -- OpenSSL framework for file encryption and integrity protection

lecture_topics: Libcrypto and application -- file encrytion/ encrypted FS / encrypted partitions

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment – using crypto primitives, centralized authentication and using PKI infrastructures.
Lab – Using OpenSSL framework/using TLS decryption and inspection tools
Assignment – Building applications using Tor/analyzing the protocol
